summary: Intermittent 429s for realtime API during nightly background sweep after split-window rollout
description:
Issue summary: BrightCart reports periodic 429 responses on realtime generation endpoints that systematically happen during a nightly background sweep job (cron-driven). Impact: interactive requests (low-latency traffic) see soft-throttling waves for ~3-5 minutes while background sweep is running. Customer sees console showing available burst credits but API returns 429s.

Observed behavior differs from their expectations after we enabled split-window refills (separate refill pools for background vs interactive). They believe background traffic should be isolated but are seeing cross-impact.

Why this ticket: gather root cause, provide mitigation steps for production, and recommend configuration guidance for split-window rollout on dedicated pools.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On BrightCart dedicated pool, schedule a background sweep job that opens 200 parallel websocket/HTTP connections to /v1/embed in a 60s window (cron job runs at 02:00 UTC).
2) Simultaneously run a small interactive load generator (50 RPS) hitting the realtime text generation route for 10 minutes, measuring 429 rate and latency.
3) Observe 429 spikes aligned to cron start and heartbeat timestamps (server-side logs should show refill epoch boundary messages).
4) Check Console -> Quota panel: burst credits appear non-zero while requests are being rejected.
logs: 2026-03-10T02:00:05Z serving-runtime[svc-11]: req_id=abc123: status=429 reason=token-exhaustion pool=interactive allocated=0
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: background sweep is incorrectly borrowing from the interactive pool due to route-weight misconfiguration after split-window flag was turned on for this tenant.
Checked refill epoch offsets on edge and origin — found edge was on a 60s epoch while origin uses 300s by default. This mismatch can cause transient double-accounting during epoch boundary handoff.

Observed ingress-proxy health-check traffic (kube liveness) being classified as background sweep because of path prefix rewrite; those probes are inflating background pool utilization during cron windows.

Correlation with Console: console-readout uses origin-side aggregated counters (post-aggregation and smoothing) so during transient epoch misalignment it can show available burst credits even while edge rejects requests — explains the apparent mismatch.
Additional trace: capture span trace https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/edge/abc123 shows rate-limiter decision path and token-bucket state at rejection time.
Ran controlled repro in staging with edge epoch aligned to origin — 429s disappeared, interactive latency preserved.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Asha Patel (Support): Customer first reported 429 waves at 02:00 UTC coinciding with their cron sweep. Requested logs and a HAR for a rejected interactive request.
2026-03-10 11:03 - BrightCart (Emily Chen): Attached HAR and annotated timeline. Noted that Console shows 110 burst credits but we still saw 429s for 4 minutes.

2026-03-10 13:45 - Liam Reynolds (SRE): Ran edge/origin epoch check and found edge was misconfigured on a 60s refill epoch. Opened INT-4221 to track internal fix for default epoch mismatch and probe classification rules.

2026-03-11 02:30 - Liam Reynolds (SRE): Applied temporary mitigation: set route override to isolate background_sweep into its own low-weight pool and changed probe path to /healthz?probe=false for BrightCart edge. Asked customer to monitor next cron run.
2026-03-11 06:05 - BrightCart (Emily Chen): Confirmed next nightly sweep did not cause interactive 429s. Noted slight increase in background sweep completion time (expected due to isolation).
resolution:
Workaround applied and documented: 1) Created an isolated background pool (route tag: background_sweep) and set weight=0.1 to prevent borrow. 2) Aligned edge refill epoch to origin (set edge.refill_epoch_seconds=300). 3) Excluded kube liveness/readiness probes from rate accounting by rewriting probe path at edge. After changes, observed no 429s in production during subsequent nightly runs.

Longer-term actions: engineering to add automatic epoch-alignment check during dedicated pool provisioning (tracked in INT-4221). Recommend customers enabling per-route pool isolation for heavy background cron jobs.
follow_up_tasks: INT-4221: Ensure edge/origin refill epoch defaults are enforced for new dedicated pools.
Create KB article: 'Isolating nightly background jobs to avoid interactive 429s' and link it in Console guidance.
Add a console health indicator to display epoch alignment status between edge and origin for each dedicated pool.
Schedule post-mortem call with BrightCart next week to review configuration and suggested queueing changes.
